what_this_is: A record of every case where a published consensus label disagreed with what the model produces, and what a human decided to do about it. It exists because the stability sweep has no memory: without this, the same drifts reappear every week as though nobody had ever looked, and a check that repeats itself unchanged is one people learn to scroll past. A decision here is not permanent — it is a statement about a specific published/model pair on a specific date. If either side moves, the decision goes stale and the sweep says so.

decisions.reason: All 44 claims are list prices, cash prices, Part D spending, international comparisons and coverage rules. Nothing opposes anything. Published as debated since 2 March 2026; wrong for five months and found by accident during unrelated work.
decisions.what_would_change_it: A claim arguing that US GLP-1 pricing is justified or comparable to peer countries would create a real opposing side.
decisions.applied_note: Corrected with map_consensus --category and logged in signal_evidence_updates by detect_changes. Published now equals current, so this no longer appears as a drift. Kept as the record that the decision was carried out, not merely made.

decisions.reason: The claims broadly agree that interventions have real but modest effects. The apparently negative finding (nudges habituate within 2-4 weeks) is a nuance about one intervention type, not a counter-position. Confirmed twice: once when re-baselining the golden set on 25 August, once on 27 August.
decisions.what_would_change_it: Evidence that a major intervention class does not work at all, rather than works weakly.
decisions.applied_note: Corrected with map_consensus --category and logged in signal_evidence_updates by detect_changes. Published now equals current, so this no longer appears as a drift. Kept as the record that the decision was carried out, not merely made.

decisions.reason: Six claims, five of them mixed-quality at 2.50-2.55. The load-bearing one says mechanisms are PROPOSED - molecular mimicry, immune activation, hypersensitivity - and the rest are observations phrased as 'suggesting'. The mechanism is not established. 'Uncertain' is the correct published label and 'consensus' would publish confidence nobody has.
decisions.what_would_change_it: A mechanism established rather than proposed, or claims that stop hedging with 'suggesting'.

decisions.reason: The studies agree the modalities are comparable (RR 1.04, similar engraftment, no significant VOC difference) AND one claim states plainly that no head-to-head randomised trials exist and indirect comparisons are limited. 'Consensus' reports the agreement and buries the reason it is worth little.
decisions.what_would_change_it: A head-to-head randomised trial. Until then the honest answer is that the comparison cannot be made.

decisions.reason: Not a label problem. Eight of eleven claims are obesity prevalence statistics (40.3% national, 23 states above 35%, state-level and demographic breakdowns, 1.9 billion by 2035). Only three concern emerging therapies. The model's 'consensus' is consensus about obesity epidemiology, which has nothing to do with what this category asks.
decisions.what_would_change_it: Re-categorising the eight prevalence claims out of 'emerging'. The label question cannot be answered until the category holds the right claims.

decisions.reason: There is a real controversy here and it is narrow: MONALEESA-2/-3/-7 and MONARCH-2 each showed significant OS benefit while PALOMA-2 and PALOMA-3 showed numerical but not significant benefit, and one claim states ribociclib is the most consistent. That is a live question about whether CDK4/6 inhibitors are interchangeable. But thirty-plus claims agree these therapies extend survival. Publishing 'debated' would tell a reader that breast cancer survival outcomes are contested, which is more misleading than the status quo. About nine claims in this category are epidemiology, not survival outcomes of therapies.
decisions.what_would_change_it: A mosaic that can carry both answers at once - 'these therapies extend survival' settled, 'palbociclib specifically' contested. One status cannot. Repeated measurement does not satisfy that condition and has not changed it: the condition was never about how confidently the engine says 'debated', it was about one status having to carry two answers.

measured_repeatedly.consequence: Five independent mappings returned 'debated' every time and 5-for/2-against every time, identically. When this hold was decided the evidence for 'debated' was two single-run readings; it is now the most repeatable measurement in the whole survey. The hold therefore no longer rests on measurement uncertainty at all. It rests entirely on an editorial judgment that publishing 'debated' would tell a reader breast cancer survival is contested when what is contested is whether CDK4/6 inhibitors are interchangeable. That judgment may well be right, but it is a judgment about reader harm and not a doubt about the engine, and it must be recorded as such so nobody later mistakes it for the latter.

decisions.reason: The published label is the shakier one. The category contains VITAL finding vitamin D supplementation did NOT reduce incidence (HR 0.96, 0.81-1.14), the FDA concluding there is 'very little credible scientific evidence' on green tea, and non-significant results for nuts and omega-3 - alongside strong positives for fibre, olive oil and soy. 'Consensus' implies these foods are agreed protective and they are not. But 'debated' on 2-of-23 side attribution is not earned either, and the real structure is that different foods have different evidence, which is not a debate.
decisions.what_would_change_it: A mosaic, or splitting the category by food. Also two near-duplicate fibre claims give 5% and 7% for the same 10g/day increment, which should be reconciled.

measured_repeatedly.consequence: 'Debated' repeated five times out of five, so the status is not a fluke and the note above that it rests on 2-of-23 side attribution is now wrong in its particulars: attribution ranged from 4 to 11 of the 23 claims. But it is right in its point. The direction never clears the decisiveness floor, so the balance classifies as a tie, and the count of claims drawn into the sides at all nearly trebles between runs while the verdict does not move. Different foods having different evidence is still the real structure, and no single status describes it.

standing_notes.note: Statuses are stable. Side attribution is not.
standing_notes.evidence: Three full sweeps of 53 categories in one day returned identical statuses every time — zero flips. Side counts moved in five of six debated categories between the first two runs alone.
standing_notes.consequence: Drift detection on status is trustworthy and the masthead figure rests on solid ground. Side counts are a sample, not a count, and must never be quoted as precise.

standing_notes.note: social-media/methodology has two attractors, not one answer with noise.
standing_notes.evidence: 43 claims, identical prompt hash, hours apart: fixture 10/3, sweep 1 gave 2/10, sweep 2 gave 3/8, sweep 3 gave 11/4. Sweeps 1 and 2 are reversals of the fixture; sweep 3 matches it within 1 on both sides. The model alternates between roughly 10-for/3-against and roughly 2-for/10-against.
standing_notes.consequence: Side-balance reversal was promoted from a warning to a failure in golden_set.py on this evidence. If it fires often, the answer is to stop publishing side counts for that category rather than to soften the check.

standing_notes.note: A default that silently narrows scope while reporting success is this codebase's recurring bug.
standing_notes.evidence: detect_changes.py defaults --issue-slug to glp1-drugs and reported COMPLETE after processing one topic when two had changed. Earlier the same day: golden_set treated an API failure as a warning and printed 'no published judgment moved' while blind to six categories; a git commit run from the wrong directory reported 'nothing to commit, working tree clean'.
standing_notes.consequence: Prefer an explicit required argument over a default, and make an unrun check fail rather than pass quietly.

standing_notes.note: A category with no stated proposition answers a different question on alternate calls.
standing_notes.evidence: social-media/methodology, 43 claims, prompt hash 7722652f9266. Eleven measurements across one day fall into two tight clusters that are near mirror images: 10/3, 11/4, 10/4, 12/3, 10/4 and ~10/3 lean FOR; 2/10, 3/8, 4/10, 3/10, 4/10 lean AGAINST. A single five-run burst flipped twice within about a minute, so it is per-call, not session or time-of-day. The verdict was 'debated' in all eleven.
standing_notes.diagnosis: The mirror-image counts show the model partitions the same claims the same way each time and then swaps which side is 'for'. The category is named 'methodology', which is a subject, not a proposition. Two near-inverse propositions fit it: 'the methodology of this literature is too weak to support claims of harm' puts Orben, Przybylski and Ferguson on the FOR side; 'social media harms teen mental health' puts Haidt and Twenge there instead. The engine's own summary states the mechanism: both camps agree the research has serious methodological problems and draw opposite conclusions from that fact.
standing_notes.consequence: This cannot be fixed by better prompting or more runs. The category needs an explicit falsifiable proposition, which is what step0_proposition.py and step0_mosaic.py were built to produce. Until then the verdict is publishable and the balance is not.

standing_notes.note: A reversal near a tie and a reversal of the axis are not the same fault, and our first guard could not tell them apart.
standing_notes.evidence: Five runs each. social-media/methodology: 10/3, 2/10, 3/8, 11/4, 4/10 — decisive leans of five to eight claims in both directions. social-media/platform_design: 6/5, 6/6, 6/7, 6/6, 6/6 — the 'for' side identical in every run, 'against' moving by one across equality. The boolean sides_stable tested only the sign of the difference and flagged both.
standing_notes.consequence: sides_balance (migration 075) replaces the boolean's reading with lean / tie / unstable. A lean counts as decisive only at 2+ claims AND more than a tenth of those attributed. A tie is a finding and gets published as an even split; only an inversion is withheld. Suppressing the tie would have been the same class of error in the other direction: hiding a real result behind our own noise.

standing_notes.note: The methodology pathology is so far unique, which is what makes the diagnosis credible.
standing_notes.evidence: Seven debated categories measured five times each. Exactly one shows mirror-image inversion. Three lean stably, three tie stably, and every one of the seven returned the same status in all five runs — 100% agreement across the board.
standing_notes.consequence: The inversion is a property of a category whose name states a subject and not a proposition, not a general property of the engine. The remedy is to give that category a proposition, not to distrust the engine. It also means the run cost is worth paying where a category is named loosely and not everywhere.

standing_notes.note: Status stability, direction stability and coverage stability are three different things and we currently measure two.
standing_notes.evidence: diet/protective_foods returned 'debated' five times out of five and a stable tie, while the number of claims drawn into either side at all ran 5, 9, 11, 5, 4 out of 23. The verdict was perfectly repeatable while what it was a verdict about was not.
standing_notes.consequence: Nothing in the pipeline notices when a run attributes half as many claims as the run before it. sides_observed makes it visible to anyone who looks, but no guard reads it. Worth a guard before side counts are ever quoted as counts.

measurements.method: eleven mappings across one day; five of them a single --runs 5 burst
measurements.reading: Two tight mirror-image clusters. The only category of the seven measured that inverts. The side lists are withheld from the row by reconcile() and the CHECK in migration 074 enforces the pairing.

The 'for' side is 6 in all five runs and never moves; only 'against' wanders by one, which straddles equality and reverses the sign of a lean that was never there. This is a well-measured tie, not methodology's axis inversion, and it is publishable as an even split. The original boolean guard called it unstable, which was a false positive of our own making.
Decisive in the same direction every run. No sign of the methodology pathology.
Decisive FOR in four of five runs, tied in the fifth, never against. Stable.
Only two of five runs clear the decisiveness floor, so this reads as a tie rather than a lean. Nothing reverses.

what_measurements_are: Repeated mappings of a single category, run with --measure-only so nothing was written to the database. These are NOT decisions and the stability sweep must not read them as such: a measurement says how consistently the engine answers, which is self-consistency and not truth. They live here because the sweep has no memory either, and because a claim that a category is unstable should be checkable against the numbers that made us say so.
